## Social caption — two free family festivals

Suggested use after access and current sources are verified; retire before Sat 19 September 11:00.

Birmingham, this weekend has buses to inspect and a whole neighbourhood to explore 🧡

SATURDAY 19 SEPTEMBER: Brum Transport Fest, 11am–5pm. Free, no booking. Classic cars, buses and family activities across city-centre squares, including Victoria, Centenary and Hippodrome Squares. An outdoor day for transport fans of all ages.

SUNDAY 20 SEPTEMBER: Moor Pool Heritage Festival, 11am–3pm. Free, no booking for the festival. Start at Moor Pool Hall, 37 The Circle, Harborne: family trails, crafts, brass music and sport tasters across the estate. Refreshments cost extra; some routes have slopes or steps.

Our pick for families with children 0–12, keeping the route short for little legs. Children need a grown-up throughout.

Saturday details: https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/brum-transport-festival/
Sunday details: https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/moor-pool-heritage-festival/

Birmingham’s weekend shortlist, 19–20 September 🧡

SATURDAY
• Brum Transport Fest: city-centre vehicles and family activities, 11am–5pm. Free, no booking.
• Helios at The Exchange: an illuminated Sun to gaze at, 8am–5pm. Free, no booking. Closed Sunday.
• Optional paid detour: Explore Blakesley, Yardley. Hall entries 11am–3pm; grounds until 4pm. £5 adult / £3 child advertised, book ahead and check checkout total.

SUNDAY
• Moor Pool Heritage Festival: trails, crafts and sport tasters, 11am–3pm. Free festival entry, no booking.
• Make a Mini Museum at Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery: 11am–3pm, free drop-in, all ages.

Children with a grown-up. The festivals welcome mixed ages; we’d especially pick the Sun and Tudor visit for curious school-age children. Bring coats for the outdoor stops.

## Friday weekend-brief email — UNSENT

Subject: Birmingham: four free plans and one Tudor detour

Preheader: Transport on Saturday, neighbourhood exploring and making on Sunday.

Hi Birmingham,

For Saturday 19 September, start with [Brum Transport Fest](https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/brum-transport-festival/), 11am–5pm, free with no booking. Or keep it short under [Helios at The Exchange](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/the-exchange/events/helios), open 8am–5pm, also free with no booking. The Exchange isn’t a Sunday option.

Sunday 20 September brings [Moor Pool Heritage Festival](https://birminghamheritageweek.co.uk/event/moor-pool-heritage-festival/), 11am–3pm: free trails, crafts and activities around the hall and estate. For indoors, [Make a Mini Museum](https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/marvellous-makers) at BMAG runs 11am–3pm, free drop-in for all ages. Stay with your children.

The optional paid choice is Saturday’s [Explore Blakesley](https://www.birminghammuseums.org.uk/events/heritage-open-day-and-birmingham-heritage-week-explore-blakesley): £5 adult / £3 child advertised, timed Hall entries 11am–3pm, grounds until 4pm. Pre-book and check the final total. It is not a free Heritage Week visit.

The festivals work for mixed-age families; the Sun and Tudor house are our picks for school-age curiosity. Moor Pool has slopes and some steps, with side wheelchair entry to the hall. Food and travel are extra.

[DoNext Birmingham](https://donext.co.uk/birmingham/)

## Weekday subscriber email — UNSENT

Intended Monday 14 September; retire before Friday 18 September 16:00. Recheck hours before later use.

Subject: Birmingham: a little space, a little deep time

Preheader: Two free indoor stops for curious children this week.

Hi Birmingham,

For a short space-themed stop, [Helios at The Exchange](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/the-exchange/events/helios), Centenary Square, is free with no booking, Monday–Saturday 8am–5pm. It’s an illuminated sculpture rather than a children’s workshop. We’d pick it particularly for ages 5–12 with a grown-up.

For fossils and crystals, [Lapworth Museum](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/cultural-attractions/lapworth-museum-of-geology/visit-us) on the university’s Edgbaston campus is free with no booking. September weekday hours are **10am–4pm**, not 5pm. That makes it better for preschool or home-educating families than a rushed after-school dash. Our suggested fit is 3–12; prams and wheelchairs are supported, with a lift to the mezzanine and baby-changing facilities. Parking is charged.
